children: Gold futures posted modest gains Thursday, helped by lower crude oil prices and a pullback in Treasury yields a day after the Federal Reserve delivered its first rate hike in three years and signaled that more tightening may still be needed.

Crude prices extended ​their recent decline to hit a one-week low as supply disruption fears eased, the dollar dropped from a seven-week high, making greenback-priced bullion more affordable for holders of other currencies, and the yield ​on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury fell to a one-week low 4.946%.

While the Fed raised rates and flagged more hikes in the coming months, the Bank of England held interest rates unchanged on Thursday, and the Bank of Japan is expected ⁠to raise rates ​to a 31-year high on Friday.

"We've been tied very closely to an inverse relationship ​with energy prices based on those inflationary pressures... Energy prices are down fairly ⁠dramatically. So it's these lower energy prices that are removing some of that pressure on ​the gold market," High Ridge Futures senior director of metals trading David Meger said in a note.

The bull market for gold could continue at some stage with underlying drivers such as central bank demand, macro uncertainty, and fiscal concerns, Pepperstone strategist Ahmad Assiri said in a note, but "the path of oil prices and their transmission into Fed policy remains the single most important variable from now until year-end."
